Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 16:15:00 -0400
Subject: Sapphire Lane - quick inventory check and proposed standby allocation

Team —

Sapphire Lane is in late-stage commercial review (see HubSpot deal SL-2028-07-19). They're asking for sizing guidance and a provisional standby while procurement finalizes terms and legal. They may push for a 6–9 month ramp and want predictable throughput for a batch/stream hybrid workload.

High-level ask: can we confirm availability for a 6-month provisional standby for the following profile, and give options & trade-offs (soft-hold vs provisional reserve vs committed)?

- Desired capacity: 4x A100 80GB-equivalent instances (single-tenant Dedicated pool)
- Target start: mid-August (flexible +/- 2 weeks)
- Ramp profile: month 1 — light POC, month 2–3 — increased traffic, month 4+ — production throughput

What I need back by EOD Monday:
1) Current free inventory that could service 4x A100-equivalent nodes in us-east-1 (and any constraints on bay / rack scheduling)
2) Recommended hold type and the operational impact (can we do a soft, zero-cost hold for 30 days while procurement finishes PO? If not, what's the minimum financial commitment we can offer?)
3) Any maintenance windows or preplanned capacity events that overlap Aug–Sep that would affect availability

I'm attaching the customer MOP draft and the initial fleet sizing sheet they shared (redacted). I'm going to loop in Evelyn to confirm SLA guardrails if we need to promise latency tiers.

Thanks —

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 18:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sapphire Lane - quick inventory check and proposed standby allocation

Kimberly —

Inventory snapshot (us-east-1, as of 2028-07-20 18:30 EDT):
- Total A100-equivalent spare nodes across dedicated fleet: 28
- Nodes currently reserved for commitments (monthly/annual): 14
- Soft-hold slots currently placed (non-billable, 30d auto-expire): 6
- Maintenance/firmware window impacting 3 racks: Aug 10–14 (can reprioritize if we take action now)

Options and trade-offs:

1) Soft-hold (recommended quick path)
- What: zero-charge marker to hold nodes for up to 30 days, auto-releases after 30d unless converted
- Pros: fastest to grant; minimal bookkeeping; customer gets option to convert to reserved commit
- Cons: other teams could convert into a hard reserve before 30d if overlapping deals escalate (we can prevent by elevating to provisional hold)

2) Provisional reserve (sales-managed, 60–90d)
- What: administrative hold with documented intent to convert; not invoiced but flagged in capacity planner; requires signed MOU or email from procurement
- Pros: better protection than soft-hold; reduces double-book risk
- Cons: operationally sticky; needs sign-off from capacity planning (Evelyn) and finance for exposure

3) Committed reservation (contractual)
- What: billed reserved capacity with SLA and capacity guarantees
- Pros: rock-solid guarantee; preferred if customer ready to commit
- Cons: requires procurement/legal, multi-month billing; reduces our flexible pool

Given the current numbers, we can grant a 30-day soft-hold immediately for 4x A100-equivalent. If the customer asks for a longer protection window, I recommend provisional reserve (60–90d) with an MOU — that will block the capacity in our planner and let us shift maintenance windows.

Operational notes:
- If we place provisional reserve, we should move the target racks out of the Aug 10–14 maintenance window; that requires 72h lead time.
- Impact to autoscaler: none if soft-hold; provisional reserve will reduce available autoscale headroom by ~14% in us-east-1 for that hardware profile.

I'll attach a short inventory export and a scheduler snapshot.

-Marcus

Summary of recommended configuration (per Marcus):
- Baseline: 4x A100 80GB-equivalent dedicated nodes (single-tenant pool)
- Start window: target mid-August (flexible)
- Recommended protection: 30-day soft-hold now, convertible to 60–90d provisional reserve upon signed MOU/intent from procurement

What we can do now:
- Place a 30-day soft-hold on the requested nodes today to give procurement breathing room; no billing for soft-hold and auto-expire after 30d
- If procurement can provide a short MOU or an email of intent, we can elevate to a provisional reserve (60–90d) which will give you stronger priority and let us rearrange maintenance windows so the Aug 10–14 window won't affect your racks

Requested next steps from Sapphire Lane:
1) Confirm you'd like us to place the 30-day soft-hold today (reply to this email)
2) If you prefer stronger protection, please share an MOU or procurement note and we'll escalate to provisional reserve and lock racks away from the Aug maintenance window
3) Share any additional throughput/latency SLOs so we can validate the sizing against SLAs

I'll attach the MOP draft we discussed and the sizing sheet for your review. If you confirm the soft-hold, Marcus will place it and issue a short internal notice to the capacity team.
